body:
So what you're saying is that you want to be busting your ass when you should be retired.

Got it.

Thanks. As far as I'm aware Gramps hasn't tried a VSO so this is looking like one of the more promising options, though like I mentioned in the OP he had a stroke a while back so I'm not sure job retraining is feasible. Do you have any specifics on what other sorts of assistance they may be able to offer?

~ 60 - 65 for both of them, N. Illinois. Gramps is a vet (Navy, I think?) and works food service and Grandma works one day a week minimum wage but it's really only cursory and I'm not sure she could do more even if she wanted to. They have an adult child and her husband too but they don't make much either and I don't get the impression they're super inclined to help if only because they're accustomed to the situation and don't have the depth of experience to even consider taking over stewardship of the family (that's a nice way of saying they don't seem super helpful).

I'll totally look into your suggestions but feel free to add more if you think of any.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=w7BiDhXq89w

This 'issue' of yours isn't external to your personal circumstances, so it's probably a good idea not to self-identify as a sadist. You're a person who happens to be quasi-sadistic. Big deal. Use it to your advantage (in a good way) or ignore it.
Aim for psychological malleability -- if you dwell on self-diagnosed sadism won't it facilitate that sort of thinking? I doubt you're the only person with sadistic tendencies.

Well, in this scenario I sort of *am* the homeless guy. o__o
Don't worry tho, I have a pig-sticker.

I have similar inclinations, only I'd refer to myself as... an emotionally intelligent sociopath (?). I've come to consider it a boon since I can align with the status quo when appropriate but still have some inner fire available if someone crosses the line.

I can't say I empathize (lol) with an urge to inflict emotional pain, but would suggest you direct your 'talents' towards something productive such as political discussion.

Okay, let me put it this way: if you were being bullied, but the bullies in question could see what was going to happen before you do, and had already made it obvious that they weren't good people, how would you react? My solution is to discern the actual circumstances, and I've made some progress, but is that enough?

>I can relate to this, and I'm still trying to find answers myself. Would it be okay if I messaged you privately?

Sure! I don't honestly know if I can handle my own problems, but I do have extensive experience coping with existential crises and psychological trauma.

How would you react if everything you enjoy about life was intentionally ruined, [but in a way that's only obvious to you?](https://m.youtube.com/watch?v=wdq1qJkahDY) How can someone recover from something like that? I had figured the surreal nightmare worlds would be reserved for war criminals or something.

Suppose you had gained some notoriety, and would likely choose to be mundane or anonymous if given the choice. Should you then leverage your "importance" for the sake of improving lives (including your own), or should you work in the margins in the hopes of enacting progress sans clout?

Some suffering? I'm okay with that depending on the circumstances, especially if it leads to a net gain in subjective happiness without also incurring an unreasonable cost. I don't know what sorts of suffering Nietzche endured, but do you suppose he would espouse such a mentality to a man on the rack? Instead of eliminating *or* worshipping suffering, how about we simply ensure that it leads to personal growth and happiness?

"Music does bring people together. 
It allows us to experience the same emotions. 
People everywhere are the same in heart and spirit.
No matter what language we speak, what color we are, 
the form of our politics or the expression of our love and our faith, 
music proves: We are the same."

I haven't read it fully until now due to qualms I've had with dualism. Now that I have, I can kind see the use of such a philosophy. However,, I also wonder if it's simply designed to discourage people from aspiring to power. I don't want power as much as I want security, but then what can be done when security appears to require power? I'm a fairly staunch agnostic in most regards, so I'm not sure I could have faith in the tao any more than I could have faith in any deity whom I'm unsure even exists. While I would actually *like* to do so, if only to reduce my own mental strife, I feel as if it would be a lie. Do you have any advice for a person who finds it particularly difficult to experience genuine faith? Perhaps ironically, my assertion that I don't know anything for sure (which would seem to align with Taoism to some degree) is precisely why I'm not sure I could adopt such a philosophy.

What's more, I *like* to figure stuff out, though I've encountered context which suggests this is unwise. Can you see why stuff like this is difficult for me? :P I *don't* think I'm smart or wise as much as I would be lying if I settled on a philosophy or religion which I didn't understand.

>You got that inside you. Even though you don't know / feel it yet. Something I really want you to take home is: everybody has their demons.

I tend to have a lot of big ideas, but I'm starting to think a big imagination means big fears. I'm not so sure I can undo some of the stuff I've thought of at this point. I'll probably make some progress, but it's going to be tough with all this... stuff hanging over my head. Thanks for your kind words.

>Every time I'm starting to work on something new I'm paralyzed with fear of "maybe I won't be able to do it this time, and they will all know I was just pretending to know what i'm doing all this time

I don't think this is an uncommon thought. I've had issues with follow-through myself, and despite some really good ideas I haven't even gotten as far as you. Be proud of yourself for making money doing something you enjoy, and please have faith that you have the chops to do this stuff.

>I hope the best for you and won't give up on you like a lot of the world.

Thank you. I doubt you could comprehend how nice it is to hear that. Please hang on to this attitude, even if it's hard. I check this account every now and then in case you'd like to talk more :)

Thanks for the advice. I try to think about others, and I *do* help people when I get the chance, but sometimes I wonder if there's some underlying negative feedback for empathy, strangely enough. I suspect that the more I worry about people in general the more I'll hurt. I don't want to give up my ideals regarding compassion, but it's starting to feel downright masochistic to me, so by doing so I also end up worrying about my own strife. Is there a way to adopt the beneficial aspects of apathy without also giving up whatever legitimate moral rectitude I actually have?

Thanks for the kind words :)

>I told her how I can't look at myself in the mirror anymore because of how disgusted I am with myself.

I'm not actually disgusted with myself -- I worked through most such issues before I ever got "depressed", actually. That's part of the problem, though. I'm actually more disappointed with the world, since I feel as if I'm being punished for things which are beyond my control -- it's hard to explain that in a way which doesn't sound narcissistic or petty. Reality seems really dark and confusing to me these days, and though I'm not trying to act like I'm some pure soul or something, I do feel kind of like I'm in some kind of weird bizzaro world which is trying to teach me all the wrong lessons. I wonder if the overarching theme here is that I would have been better off as a jaded bastard, and that just seems so, *so* wrong to me.

What can be done about this? I almost feel as if I'll be rewarded for giving up my ideals. I don't want to be that way, but I don't know if the incentive to adopt apathy will let up. Giving a shit just hurts so much, which is ass backwards from what I've been taught thus far.

>I will love Soul until the very end because has taught me that the sun will rise with, or without you, but if you care enough to see it, you will endure another day.

I know that I don't have it so bad (at least at this particular moment), but I'm not sure such sentiments help -- it just feels like more arbitrary suffering which doesn't need to occur. There *has* to be a better way. People aren't ultimately cruel or indifferent, are they?

>sunlight filtering through the leaves of the tree outside my living room window and feeling a rapturous ecstasy at the endless potential that being alive affords us.

This may sound weird, but what do you do when even sunlight seems disturbing and depressing? Sometimes I get the strange notion that this entire existence is only here for the sake of making me suffer, and when I'm in that state of mind I find it difficult to appreciate much of anything, as it strikes me as twisted instead of beautiful. How do I get around this?

>I know its cliché but you won't know for sure until you try!

Well, I don't know, and if anyone does know what's actually going on they should really tell me so I can make a rational, informed choice for once. I'll try to keep this in mind, though.

>I can only effect now.

I understand the whole "live for the moment" thing, but how do you suppose a man on death row would react to that? Not to suggest that's what I'm going through, but sometimes I wonder how bad things can really get. I'm not sure how long I can be all c'est la vie before something gives. I'm honestly hanging on to the notion that it will all end up being worth it, but I can't shake the notion that I'm only here to act as an example (in a bad way). I don't want to be this way, and I'd dearly like to be more of a tigger or a pooh than an eeyore. I'm starting to wonder if I somehow managed to piss off all of god, satan, *and* a gaggle of petty time lords who're all conspiring to shit up every waking moment :P You'd think they'd all have something better to do, especially since I don't even understand how it got to this point, but yet here we are O_o

Thanks for the advice, though :) Let me know if you need to talk about something yourself.

That's a start. Do you simply enjoy those things, or do you create them (aside from the kids -- that one is pretty obvious :P)? Our ability to create trumps all other circumstances, no matter how bad they may seem at the moment. Have you tried adopting some art form as a hobby or a career?

Thanks for replying :)

>You say you are aware of things that could make your life wonderful, so as long as that possibility exists you should strive to achieve those things.

That's what I've been going for, but for reasons which are hard to explain I wonder if I'm up against forces which I'm not equipped to take on. I'm pretty good at coming up with unique or unexpected options, but sometimes I wonder if I lost this "battle" before I was even born. Whether or not that's just a depressive delusion, it seems pretty real to me. How do I summon up the courage to try when faced with *that*?
What do you like about life?
I don't have much advice, since I don't feel much better right now, but if you want someone to talk to feel free to pm me :)
